install_root_note: One path, holding a git checkout, and branches are switched in it. There used to be a second profile, 'randi-main', identical to this one but for this line, so that two branches could each have code on the cluster without either overwriting the other. That made a second copy of every fact on this page — the modules, the excluded nodes, the resource classes — free to disagree with the ones here, and it was already 96% the same file when it was found. A checkout does the same job without the copy: `git checkout` swaps the tracked code and leaves the built environments alone, since those are ignored by git and untracked files survive a checkout. What it does not do is let two branches be current at once. Whoever checks out last wins, and the client refuses to submit when its catalog entry differs from the one here, naming what this is checked out at so the refusal says whose code is installed rather than that two digests differ.
description: Randi, the collaborator HPC. The default target for cluster work. Hierarchical module environment, so several modules need a prerequisite loaded first.
notes: Three properties of this host drive the settings above. /tmp is mounted noexec, so staging and singularity temp files both have to live under scratch rather than the default temp directory. The containers directory sits on GPFS which is also noexec, so images are read from scratch. And go must be loaded before singularity, which is why the preamble has two lines in that order. Module names for julia 1.9.0 and R 4.4.1 are not listed here because every kernel runs inside a container; they matter only for a native run. The executor block is harvested from the working Nextflow configuration. Those values were arrived at by running the pipeline rather than by reading anything: the excluded nodes are three machines found to fail, symlink in and move out is a GPFS optimisation, and lenient caching accommodates unreliable timestamps on that filesystem. None of it is recoverable by rewriting from scratch. The image path includes a 'cancer' directory that was introduced during an unrelated reorganisation; an older Nextflow config still points one level above it and would not find the images.

executor.preamble_note: What the driver itself needs before it can start, which is not what a task needs. The task preamble at the top of this file loads python and singularity so run.py can work; these four load the engine. Nextflow will not start without openjdk loaded first, and neither module is visible until then.
executor._exclude_note: Nodes observed to fail in practice. cri22cn084 cannot resolve the running user inside a container, so singularity aborts before the kernel starts. Found 2026-08-08 while running work from this tree; which capability it was is not a property of the node, and naming it made this machine's profile answer to one domain's catalog.
executor.partition_note: tier1q is 147 nodes with a ten day limit. Alternatives: tier2q, express (6h).

resource_classes._note: Keyed by a contract's resources.bound_by, so a capability never names a number and a site never names a capability. Every value below is what this repository's own submission scripts already request, except where basis says otherwise.

memory.basis: run_phylo_node_extract.sh and run_spatial_optimize.sh both request 32G; the longer of their two limits is taken.

cpu.basis: run_ripley_k.sh requests 16G for an hour, and the four cpus match the -@ 4 that the bootstrap support step already passes.

walltime.basis: No precedent in the repository: the only capability bound this way has no submission script here, so there is nothing to take a figure from. It is a guess and should be replaced by a measurement. It named that capability until 2026-08-16, which made this machine's profile depend on one domain's catalog for no gain — the sentence is true whichever capability it is.

io.basis: No precedent in the repository. Work that streams a file through and writes another needs neither cores nor memory, so this takes the trivial class's shape with more wall time, since throughput here follows the filesystem rather than the node. Replace with a measurement once one large sample has been bundled.

toolchain.note: The module tree is hierarchical: nothing but dmd, gcc, go, intel, llvm and openjdk is visible until a compiler is loaded. Python, R and the rest appear only after gcc. The login node default is 3.6.8, which is too old to run the tooling here, so the module is not optional.

conda_base_note: Pinned by the gcc/12.1.0 + miniconda3/24.9.2 module pair. A domain says it needs a conda environment; where conda itself lives is this machine.
env_strip_note: This host's default LD_LIBRARY_PATH ships a Java 8 libjli that breaks a newer java in any conda environment, which kills Trimmomatic inside KneadData. Removing the entry is a property of the machine, so it is recorded here rather than inside a pipeline.
login_nodes_note: Hosts that exist to submit work, not to do it. The runner refuses to execute here, so the rule holds for every domain rather than for whichever pipeline remembered to check. ANALYSIS_ALLOW_LOGIN_NODE=1 overrides it.
reference_roots_note: Where shared reference data and package caches live on this machine. A domain says which database version it needs; this says where databases are kept, and keeps a cache off the small home quota. Neither half means anything without the other, which is why they were one file and had to stop being one.
artifact_root_note: Results live beside the data they came from, on shared storage rather than scratch, because a run record outlives the run. A capability never names this: the store allocates a directory and hands it back.
data_root_note: Where this machine's study data lives. Discovery asks each site what it holds rather than one machine answering for all of them, so this is randi's answer and nobody else's.
references_note: What this machine provides that belongs to no study and is produced by no run. A capability names one and each site says where it keeps it, so an entry never carries a path.
